title: 1-gang steel device box, 3 × 2 × 2-1/2 in, with cable clamps

sources.citation: game-design: the 3 × 2 × 2-1/2 in sheet-steel device (switch) box, a common trade designation for one-gang outlet boxes (sheet-steel outlet boxes are listed to UL 514A and described by NEMA OS 1, cited by number). The designation's nominal 2 in wide, 3 in tall and 2-1/2 in deep are taken as the inside dimensions, rounded to whole millimetres (51 × 76 × 64 mm), with 2 mm drawn walls (sheet steel of about 1.6 mm, rounded up) on the sides and back, so the outside is 55 × 80 × 66 mm. Unverified: no manufacturer drawing was read for this entry; electrical-realism-reviewer to check it against public dimension drawings of the class and relabel it real-world if it holds.

game-design: computed from the inside dimensions above as a plain rectangular volume, 51 × 76 × 64 = 248064 mm³ (about 15.1 in³). It is the drawn box's volume, not a marked volume and not from any code table; a real box's marked volume is smaller (rounded corners, clamps, ears). P4's box fill reads it.

game-design: one device yoke (one wiring device per gang, UL 514A by number). A mounted device's origin sits at the inside back-lower-left corner (2, 2, 2) facing out of the box (+z), so a device fills the gang from the back wall; P4's devices are sized to the gang.

game-design: a pryout behind each of the two internal cable clamps (top and bottom, toward the front, one cable each, the box clamps it) and three 1/2 in trade-size knockouts (top, bottom and back, one connector each), the usual openings of a steel device box with clamps; positions are on the outside wall faces and are not taken from a product drawing.
game-design: nailed or screwed to the side of a stud by a bracket (common practice for device boxes in wood framing); it takes its full width along the stud.
